## Summary

I added the `include_environment_context` flag (defaulting to `true` to preserve existing behavior) across the config layers and gated the actual injection of the `<environment_context>` tag on it.

**`codex-rs/core/src/config/mod.rs`**
- Added `pub include_environment_context: bool` to the `Config` struct.
- Added `pub include_environment_context: Option<bool>` to the `ConfigToml` struct (on-disk representation).
- Added resolution logic mirroring the existing `include_*_instructions` pattern: `config_profile.include_environment_context.or(cfg.include_environment_context).unwrap_or(true)`, so the profile value takes precedence over the top-level config, and both default to `true` when absent.
- Wired the resolved value into the `Config` struct construction.

**`codex-rs/core/src/config/profile.rs`**
- Added `pub include_environment_context: Option<bool>` to `ConfigProfile` for profile-level overrides.

**`codex-rs/core/src/codex.rs`** (initial context build)
- Wrapped the push of `EnvironmentContext::...serialize_to_xml()` into `contextual_user_sections` (the user-role message) in `if turn_context.config.include_environment_context { ... }`. When `false`, no `<environment_context>` tag or content is added.

- Added an early `return None` in `build_environment_update_item` when `!next.config.include_environment_context`, so subsequent-turn environment diffs are also suppressed — matching the existing pattern used by `build_permissions_update_item`.
